observations.question: What fast-charging subsidy rate, per-station cap and station count does the 2025 policy state, and are slow chargers incentivized?

result.answer:
Karnataka — source cutoff: 2026-09-23.

Prototype source review is pending; current availability and individual eligibility are not verified.

- Fast‑charging stations for 2‑wheelers, 3‑wheelers, cars and buses receive a capital subsidy of 25 % of the station cost, with a maximum subsidy of Rs 10,00,000 per station, and the policy earmarks up to 500 such stations for incentive. [S2](https://investkarnataka.co.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Clean-mobility-policy.pdf#page=22)
- Slow‑charging stations are not covered by any incentive; the policy states there are no incentives for slow‑charging stations. [S2](https://investkarnataka.co.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Clean-mobility-policy.pdf#page=22)

Sources:

- [S2: Karnataka — Karnataka Clean Mobility Policy 2025–2030, PDF page 22](https://investkarnataka.co.in/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Clean-mobility-policy.pdf#page=22)

4.3.2 Incentives for Charging and Hydrogen stations for all Zones

There are 3 types of charging stations for electric vehicles:
 Fast charging
 Slow charging
 Battery switching/swapping

For hydrogen vehicles, there are hydrogen stations.

4.3.2.1 Fast charging stations for all Zones.

All fast charging stations for 2W, 3W, cars and buses will be offered the following
incentives:
